questions.question: A train crosses two platforms of length 1000 m and 600 m in 80 seconds and 60 seconds respectively. What is the length of the train?
questions.solution:
Let the length of the train be x m.

As we know,

Speed = (x + 1000)/80 ---(1)

Speed = (x + 600)/60 ---(2)

From equation (1) and equation (2)

(x + 1000)/80 = (x + 600)/60

⇒ 3 (x + 1000) = 4 (x + 600)

⇒ 3x + 3000 = 4x + 2400

⇒ 4x – 3x = 3000 – 2400

⇒ x = 600

Length of the train is 600 m.

questions.question: A train, 250 m long, passes a railway platform 200 m long, in 45 s with a uniform speed. What is the time (in seconds) taken by the train to pass a man cycling in the direction of the train at a speed of 6 km/h?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of train = Total Distance ÷ Time = (250 + 200) ÷ 45 = 10 m/s.

Speed of man = 6 × (5 ÷ 18) = 5/3 m/s.

Relative speed in same direction = 10 − 5/3 = 25/3 m/s.

Time to pass the man = Train Length ÷ Relative Speed = 250 ÷ (25/3).

Time = 250 × (3 ÷ 25) = 30 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Speed of man = 6 km/h

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = Speed of Train − Speed of Object

Time to cross a moving object = Train Length ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance covered to cross the platform = Length of train + Length of platform

⇒ Total distance = 250 + 200 = 450 m

⇒ Speed of train = 450 ÷ 45 = 10 m/s

⇒ Speed of man in m/s = 6 × (5 ÷ 18) = 5/3 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 10 − 5/3 = (30 − 5) ÷ 3 = 25/3 m/s

⇒ Time taken to cross the man = Length of train ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time = 250 ÷ (25/3) = (250 × 3) ÷ 25

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

Train Crossing Rules

questions.question: Two trains starting at the same time from two stations 300 km apart and going in opposite directions cross each other at a distance of 180 km from one of the stations. What is the ratio of speeds of faster train to slower train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When travel time is constant, Speed is directly proportional to Distance.

Distance covered by the faster train = 180 km

Distance covered by the slower train = 300 − 180 = 120 km

Ratio of speeds = Ratio of distances = 180 : 120

Speed Ratio = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance between the two stations = 300 km

Distance covered by the faster train before crossing = 180 km

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bab2e62bc296011a93d54715b26f8bdf935eabac2f62a02ba88e5fae74c5ce54.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by the slower train = 300 − 180 = 120 km

⇒ Since both trains start at the same time and cross each other, the time traveled by both is perfectly equal.

⇒ Let the time taken be t hours.

⇒ Speed of faster train = 180 ÷ t

⇒ Speed of slower train = 120 ÷ t

⇒ Ratio of speeds = (180 ÷ t) : (120 ÷ t)

⇒ Ratio of speeds = 180 : 120

⇒ Speed ratio = 3 : 2

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). The time taken for them to meet is Total Distance ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Constant Time Principle

When the travel time is constant for two moving bodies, the ratio of their speeds is directly proportional to the ratio of the distances they cover: S₁ ÷ S₂ = D₁ ÷ D₂.

Constant Distance Principle

When the distance covered is constant for two moving bodies, their speeds are inversely proportional to the time taken: S₁ ÷ S₂ = T₂ ÷ T₁.
</p

questions.question: Two trains are running in opposite direction with the same speed. If the length of each train is 160 metres and they cross each other in 32 seconds, then what is the speed of each train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of each train = 160 metres

Time taken to cross each other = 32 seconds

Both trains are running in opposite directions with the same speed.

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = (Total Distance) / Time

Speed of each train = Relative Speed / 2

**Calculation:**

Total Distance = 160 + 160 = 320 metres

Relative Speed = 320 / 32

Relative Speed = 10 m/s

Speed of each train = 10 / 2 = 5 m/s

Convert m/s to km/h:

Speed of each train = 5 × 18/5 = 18 km/h

**The speed of each train is 18 km/h.**

Time taken to cross = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 350 ÷ (175/9) = (350 × 9) / 175 = 18 seconds.

Converting seconds to minutes = 18 ÷ 60 = 0.3 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.3 minutes.**

questions.question: A train takes 1 hour 30 minutes to travel between two stations P and Q. If it travels at (5)/(6) of its usual speed, how long will it take to travel between P and Q?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by the train to travel from P and Q = 1 hour 30 minutes 

**Formula used:**

Distance/Speed = Time 

When the distance is constant, Time = 1/speed 

**Calculation:**

Let the usual speed be = 6 units

⇒ Reduced speed = 6 × 5/6 = 5 units

Time taken by the train with usual speed = 1 hour 30 minutes 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6fc62a722eb08edc4e2ea907b7dc8bcbc8ac14e07c36292e3d2f64feadcead9b.png] 

So, 5 = 3/2 hours 

⇒ 6 = 3/2 × 6/5 

⇒ 6 = 1 hour 48 minutes 

**∴ Time taken to travel from P to Q with reduced speed is 1 hour 48 minutes.**

questions.question: Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 50 km/h and 110 km/h. The length of one train is 500 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 12 seconds. The length (in m) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in opposite directions = (50 + 110) × 5/18 = 160 × 5/18 = 400/9 m/s

Total distance covered in 12 s = (400/9) × 12 = 1600/3 ≈ 533.33 m

Length of second train = Total distance − Length of first train

Length of second train = 533.33 − 500 = 33.33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Speed of first train, S₁ = 50 km/h

Speed of second train, S₂ = 110 km/h

Length of first train, L₁ = 500 m

Time taken to cross, T = 12 s

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂ (opposite directions)

Total Distance (L₁ + L₂) = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 50 + 110 = 160 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 160 × (5 / 18) = 400 / 9 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = Speed × Time = (400 / 9) × 12

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Unit Conversion Rule

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a train crosses a pole or a standing man, the distance covered equals the length of the train itself.
</p

questions.question: A train of length 442 metres crosses an electric pole in 13 seconds and crosses another train of the same length travelling in opposite direction in 17 seconds. What is the speed of the second train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of the 1st train = 442 ÷ 13 = 34 m/s

Total distance when crossing each other = 442 + 442 = 884 m

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 884 ÷ 17 = 52 m/s

Speed of the 2ⁿd train = Relative speed − Speed of 1st train

⇒ 52 − 34 = 18 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 18 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Time to cross the electric pole (t₁) = 13 s

**Calculations:**

⇒ S₁ = 442 ÷ 13 = 34 m/s

When the two trains cross each other in opposite directions:

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 442 + 442 = 884 m

⇒ Relative Speed = Total Distance ÷ t₂

⇒ S₁ + S₂ = 884 ÷ 17

⇒ 34 + S₂ = 52

⇒ S₂ = 52 − 34

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂) because they are covering the total distance together.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, the faster object covers extra distance to overtake the slower one, making their relative speed the difference of their speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Train Crossing a Point Object

When a train crosses a stationary pole, standing man, or a tree, the total distance traveled is simply equal to the length of the train itself (Distance = L).

Train Crossing a Lengthy Object

When a train crosses a platform, a bridge, or another train, the total distance covered to clear it completely is the sum of their lengths (Distance = L₁ + L₂).
</p

questions.question: A 725 m long train passes through a 235 m long tunnel in 48 sec. Find the speed of the train.
questions.solution:

A 725 m long train passes through a 235 m long tunnel in 48 sec.

Speed = Distance / Time

**Calculation:**

Total distance = 725 m + 235 m

⇒ Total distance = 960 m

Speed = Total distance / Time

⇒ Speed = 960 m / 48 sec = 20 m/s

Speed (in km/h) = Speed (in m/s) × 18/5

⇒ Speed = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Two trains start at the same time from two stations and proceed towards each other at speeds 88 km/h and 75 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 65 km more than the other. What is the distance (in km) between the two stations?
questions.solution:
**Formula:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Concept:**

The time remains constant for the trains while the distance varies. We would use this concept to solve the question.

**Calculation:**

Let the time after which the trains meet be "t".

Distance traveled by 1st train during "t" = 88 × t

Distance traveled by 2nd train during "t" = 75 × t

According to the question-

⇒ 88t - 75t = 65 km

⇒ 13t = 65 km

∴ t = 5 hrs

Distance between the two station = (88 + 75) × 5 = 163 × 5 = 815 km

∴ **The distance between the stations is 815 km.**

questions.question: A train running at 75 km/hr crosses another train running at 30 km/hr in the same direction in 108 seconds. If the length of the fast-moving train is 950 m, then what is the length (in m) of the slow-moving train?

Length of slow train = Total distance − Length of fast train.

Length of slow train = 1350 − 950 = 400 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

questions.question: Two trains of equal lengths take 13 seconds and 26 seconds, respectively, to cross a pole. If these trains are moving in the same direction, then how long will they take to cross each other?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Train A takes 13 seconds to cross a pole.

Train B takes 26 seconds to cross a pole.

**Concept:**

Speed = Distance / Time

When two trains are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their speeds.

**Solution:**

Let the length of each train be L.

⇒ Speed of train A = L/13, speed of train B = L/26.

When the two trains cross each other, the total distance covered is 2L (length of train A + length of train B).

Relative speed of the two trains = speed of train A - speed of train B = L/13 - L/26 = L/26.

Time taken to cross each other = total distance / relative speed = 2L / (L/26) = 52 seconds.

**Hence, the two trains take 52 seconds to cross each other.**

questions.question: If the ratio among the time taken by three cars to travel a certain distance is 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5, then the ratio of speeds of these cars will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of time taken by three cars = 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5

**Formula Used:**

Speed ∝ 1/Time (If distance is constant)

**Calculation:**

Let the speeds of the cars be S₁, S₂, and S₃ respectively.

Let the times taken by the cars be 2t, 3t, and 5t respectively.

Since speed = distance/time, if the distance is constant, then speed is inversely proportional to time.

Therefore, S₁ ∶ S₂ ∶ S₃ = 1/(2t) ∶ 1/(3t) ∶ 1/(5t)

⇒ S₁ ∶ S₂ ∶ S₃ = 1/2 ∶ 1/3 ∶ 1/5

To remove the fractions, multiply each term by the LCM of the denominators (2, 3, 5) which is 30.

⇒ S₁ ∶ S₂ ∶ S₃ = (30 × 1/2) ∶ (30 × 1/3) ∶ (30 × 1/5)

⇒ S₁ ∶ S₂ ∶ S₃ = 15 ∶ 10 ∶ 6

**The ratio of the speeds of these cars is 15 ∶ 10 ∶ 6.**

When a train crosses a stationary point object like a man, a pole, or a tree, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train alone.

Crossing an Extended Object

questions.question: Two trains of equal length take 10 s and 20 s, respectively, to cross a pole. If these trains are moving in the same direction, then how long will they take to cross each other?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Two trains of equal length take 10 s and 20 s, respectively, to cross a pole.

Speed = Distance / Time

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = Difference of Speeds

Time taken to cross each other = (Sum of Lengths) / (Relative Speed)

**Calculation:**

Let the length of each train be L.

Speed of first train = L / 10

Speed of second train = L / 20

Relative Speed = (L / 10) - (L / 20)

⇒ Relative Speed = (2L - L) / 20

⇒ Relative Speed = L / 20

Time taken to cross each other = (2L) / (L / 20)

⇒ Time taken = 2L × 20 / L

⇒ Time taken = 40 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

questions.question: Two trains running towards each other on parallel tracks, at speeds of 45 km/hr and 51 km/hr, take 21 seconds to cross each other. If the length of one train is 290 m, then the length (in m) of the other train is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Train 1 = 45 km/hr.

Speed of Train 2 = 51 km/hr.

Time taken to cross each other = 21 seconds.

Length of Train 1 = 290 meters.

**Formula Used:**

Total distance covered = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2.

Relative speed = Speed of Train 1 + Speed of Train 2 (since they are moving towards each other).

Distance = Speed × Time.

**Calculation:**

Convert the speed of both trains from km/hr to m/s:

Speed of Train 1 = 45 km/hr = 45 × (1000 m / 3600 s) = 12.5 m/s.

Speed of Train 2 = 51 km/hr = 51 × (1000 m / 3600 s) = 14.17 m/s.

Relative speed = 12.5 m/s + 14.17 m/s = 26.67 m/s.

Calculate the total distance covered when they cross each other:

Total distance = Relative speed × Time = 26.67 m/s × 21 s = 560.07 meters.

Let the length of Train 2 be L meters. Then:

Total distance = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2 = 290 m + L m = 560.07 m.

Solving for L:

290 m + L m = 560.07 m.

L = 560.07 m - 290 m.

L = 270.07 meters.

**Therefore, the length of the other train is approximately 270 meters.**
